scenarioSurface.capabilityName: Obtain governed speech media from the bound narration provider

input.text: one projected speech generation invocation under the declared provider authority

event.text: the governed exchange is performed once under the declared attempt authority

outcome.text: one observation carries the raw provider response with its audio payload or its exact failure disposition, request and response hashes, provider identity, and timing, and no retry or substitution occurs beyond the declared attempt authority

scenarioSurface.notes:
The narration capability declares the semantic requirement
  generate-speech-audio. This capability realizes it: one authorized
  narration generation request in, one attributable speech media testimony
  out, through the bound speech provider.

  The provider is replaceable. This capability declares what speech media
  must be produced — an audio modality with decodable bytes — and what
  testimony the provider must return. The endpoint, model identity, wire
  protocol, and voice realization are realization authority bound beneath
  it, never semantics declared here. A different admitted provider
  satisfying the same contract is a rebinding, not a new capability.

  Speech generation descends into one declared speech generation slot. The
  slot is provider-neutral here: what realizes it is bound beneath this
  capability.

  The boundary fails closed and is never collapsed. A provider that returns
  no audio modality has produced no speech media and is held as absent
  modality. An empty or undecodable payload is held as unusable rather than
  materialized as silence. Only a decodable audio payload with its provider
  identity, request and response hashes, attempt count, and timing becomes
  speech media testimony.

  Model output remains untrusted testimony. Obtaining speech media
  establishes no admission, no fidelity claim, and no artifact existence.

value.boundedTestimonyUse: Cell solution candidates were used only as bounded testimony where their expressions are well-formed; junction dispositions and carrier mappings derive deterministically from the reviewed feature and the admitted blueprint. The project-speech-generation-request candidate proposed a platform-capability.http.v1 port binding; the assembled capability instead descends through the declared project-model-provider-protocol-slot bound as sda-projected-capability-invocation-port.v2 per the admitted blueprint's provider-slot node 006. The observe-governed-speech-exchange candidate proposed a governed-http-request platform binding; the assembled capability instead descends through the declared speech-provider-exchange-slot bound as sda-projected-capability-invocation-port.v2 per the admitted blueprint's provider-slot node 002.
assemblyOperations: project-speech-generation-request descends into the project-model-provider-protocol-slot (sda-projected-capability-invocation-port.v2, project-model-provider-protocol) and carries the returned provider wire request into the speech-generation-invocation carrier without credential bytes and without provider-specific schema knowledge leaking into the caller

observe-governed-speech-exchange descends into the speech-provider-exchange-slot (sda-projected-capability-invocation-port.v2, speech-provider) and computes request and response hashes over the canonical wire request and the raw provider response, deriving the SPEECH_EXCHANGE_OBSERVED observation that retains provider identity, hashes, attempt count, timing, and the raw response

resolve-speech-media-disposition derives NARRATION_MEDIA_RETURNED | PROVIDER_MODALITY_ABSENT | PROVIDER_PAYLOAD_UNUSABLE from the observation alone: a raw response without an audio modality is held as absent modality, an empty or undecodable payload is held as unusable, and only a decodable payload becomes media testimony carrying the raw payload bytes and the sha256 content digest computed over the decoded bytes

the root scenario composes project -> observe -> disposition through the admitted blueprint's route; the disposition junction is realized as the root's terminal transformation port and its three branch routes surface as the root scenario's declared outcome variants
